summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic intolerance was admitted for worsening lightheadedness, chest pressure, nausea, and dehydration over five days. He presented proactively due to concern for renal complications from poor oral intake. In the emergency department, he received IV fluids with symptom improvement. Evaluation showed no acute cardiac injury, with normal troponins and unchanged EKG. Chest imaging revealed no acute pathology. He was treated with over four liters of IV normal saline, which corrected orthostasis and improved renal function. His symptoms, including chest pain, abdominal discomfort, and pleuritic pain, resolved with rehydration. He was discharged home in stable condition with a new prescription for ondansetron for breakthrough nausea and instructions to maintain hydration and follow up with cardiology and neurology.
